children: Arabica coffee futures on the ICE exchange hit a fresh 10-week low on Wednesday given benign weather in Brazil and surging exports, while raw sugar hit a two-week trough.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
fell 0.7% to $2.8170 per lb at 1147 GMT, having hit a 10-week low of $2.8120 on Monday.
* "ICE stock levels remain low, but the market is being pressured by reports of strong exports out of Brazil and good growing weather for the 2027 crop," said broker ADMIS.
* Exchange arabica stocks (KC-TOT-TOT) are currently at a 27-year low of 217,646 bags, data shows.
* Against that, top grower Brazil's green coffee exports in the first two weeks of September stood at a daily average of some 13,500 metric tons, up 51.5%, data showed.
* Meanwhile, the weather in Brazil has been favourable of late and new crop flowering is progressing well, dealers said.
* Robusta coffee
fell 1.8% to $3,418 a metric ton.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
slipped 0.3% to 17.88 cents per lb.
* Oil prices slipped, tempting cane mills in Brazil and India to produce more sugar and less ethanol, a cane-based biofuel.
* Sugar has lost some ground after its recent run-up to a 16-month high, but remains underpinned by potential production declines in India, the European Union and Thailand, dealers said.
* France is set for its smallest sugar beet harvest since the 1970s after heatwaves and drought shrivelled crops in the EU's biggest agricultural producer, the farm ministry said.
* October white sugar
fell 0.4% to $524.20 a ton.

* The front month white sugar contract (LSUV6) expired on Tuesday, down 0.5% at $522.30. Deliveries against the expiration of the October contract totalled 9,987 lots, or 499,350 metric tons, according to preliminary information from sugar traders.
COCOA
* London cocoa
was little changed at £4,476 per ton.

* Cocoa buyers in No. 2 grower Ghana are owed about 4 billion cedi ($349 million) by regulator COCOBOD for last season's crop and want it paid before the new crop year begins, an industry body told Reuters.
* Ivory Coast's cocoa grind, a measure of demand, rose 21.3% year-on-year in August to 47,646 metric tons of beans, industry data from the world's top cocoa grower showed.
* New York cocoa
fell 0.3% to $6,029 a ton.
